hypothesis: A single label-free continuous DDPM denoiser trained on the full 110-score corpus can start from noise and refine toward a plausible whole-score window, and can reconstruct masked measures of held-out scores better than silence / marginal-frequency / persistence baselines without collapsing to silence or a single repeated column. This is the whole-score, no-labels generalization of the fractal_harmony_v1 refinement probe.

representation.note: Onset roll (first cell of each note only), kept sparse (~0.2% active). Time is meter-normalized so downbeats align across time signatures. Instrument family is a keyword classification of the Partitura part name; unclassified parts fall back to low_strings and are counted. The roll is built only from already-projected Partitura observation facts; MusicXML/MIDI/audio materialization stays in Ruby Partitura.

training.split_source: manifest lineage split (train 79 / validation 16 / test 15 scores)

task.name: masked_measure_reconstruction
task.mask_shape: contiguous centered block across all channels
task.conditioning: RePaint anchor re-imposes the unmasked context every reverse step

honesty: The roll is ~99.8% empty, so accuracy is meaningless; the reported signal is active-cell F1 on masked cells only.
Persistence (time-copy) is the mandatory strong baseline: orchestral music repeats locally, and a denoiser that only memorizes repetition should not be credited.
A learned advantage on validation must also hold on the unseen-lineage test split to count as generalization.
Unconditional samples must land in the authentic density and repetition band; collapse to silence or to one repeated column is a failure even if masked-F1 looks good.
This is a generation primitive only: it is not a critic, a selection policy, an RL reward, or a materialized audition. Materialization and human review remain downstream, deferred work.
